correctness.rationale: Exact scalar row projection resets the iterate to d_i/s_i; this gives the all-q distribution formula at every positive step. For beta<q a near-zero row yields divergence; at equality the supremum m follows by bounding numerator and denominator; for beta>q strict Jensen concavity reduces all row geometries to one equal-weak parameter, whose derivative has a unique root and strict global maximum. The 3-by-2 witness has singular values 1 and sqrt(2+epsilon^2), only one bounded corrupt datum, exact q-error and sharp tail. Standalone checker passed 9,048 exact-rational and 232,920 finite floating-point supplementary assertions; neither finite set is the proof.

value.rationale: The problem directly quantifies how projected norm-power sampling controls amplified errors from nearly redundant yet corrupted measurements, under the natural normalization of at least one unit informative projected row and bounded response error. The exact all-order minimax frontier, unique equal-weak-row worst geometry and critical endpoint provide a calibration rule and tight high-probability failure envelope at classical squared-norm sampling, even when the original least-squares matrix is uniformly conditioned. This is a complete natural reliability classification rather than a mere isolated negative example.
